strings.name: Federico Faggin
strings.summary: Federico Faggin developed silicon-gate technology at Fairchild, then led chip implementation at Intel, creating the 4004 with Hoff, Mazor and Shima. He cofounded Zilog and Synaptics, advancing Z80 and touch interfaces, and later supported consciousness research. His engineering achievements depended on multiple designers and teams, rather than a single inventor.

strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to early commercial microprocessor design and semiconductor technology, with foundational influence on personal computing and digital electronics.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Integrating processors on chips
strings.highlights.h1.text: He led 4004 circuit design and implementation with architecture and logic-design collaborators.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Entrepreneurship and interfaces
strings.highlights.h2.text: He cofounded Zilog and Synaptics, developing microprocessor, touchpad and touchscreen businesses.

strings.timeline.t1.text: The institution announced him as a 2026 full member.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Consciousness research foundation
strings.timeline.t2.text: With Elvia, he established a foundation to support consciousness research beyond his engineering work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: National technology medal
strings.timeline.t3.text: He shared the 2009 US National Medal of Technology and Innovation with Hoff and Mazor; presentation took place in 2010.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Cofounding Synaptics
strings.timeline.t4.text: With Carver Mead and others, he developed the company that later expanded touchpad and touchscreen products.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Cofounding Zilog
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Ralph Ungermann he created the chip company, later conceiving and leading Z80 development.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Intel 4004 introduced
strings.timeline.t6.text: The general-purpose commercial microprocessor developed with Hoff, Mazor and Shima reached the market.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Developing silicon gates
strings.timeline.t7.text: At Fairchild he advanced MOS silicon-gate technology for denser chip designs.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Physics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He graduated from Padua and then worked in the semiconductor industry.
